samples.summary: Untrusted finding text (evidence/summary/prose) is rendered verbatim into the App-posted PR comment without neutralising the hidden-comment markers other agent scripts key on — a body containing `<!-- agent-metrics-summary -->` makes the very next step of the same job delete the review comment (and its throttle marker).
samples.evidence: `blockingEvidence` (review-comment.mjs:98) now inlines `f.evidence` verbatim (only re-indented), and `renderReviewComment` inlines `l.summary` prose (line 221) and finding summaries; none of these are scrubbed of `<!-- ... -->` markers. `evidence` is a new field on this channel — the old fallback path rendered only `file` + `summary` via severity.mjs::section, so this diff materially widens the free-text surface. The rendered region is published as the App-authored comment (agent-review-on-demand.yml:594-601). Immediately afterwards the SAME job runs `metrics.mjs summarize` (agent-review-on-demand.yml:642), which at metrics.mjs:899 does `if ((c.body||'').includes(SUMMARY_MARKER)) safeDeleteComment(c.id)` over EVERY comment with no author check, and at metrics.mjs:846/908-915 parses+sweeps any body containing `<!-- agent-metric `. Attack: a fork PR author plants that literal string where a lens will quote it as evidence (trivially: any finding about metrics.mjs quoting its own marker constant, or a prompt-injected file), and the bot silently deletes its own review comment. Because the deleted body also carries the `<!-- agent-review:<sha> -->` dedup marker checked at agent-review-on-demand.yml:91-96, the per-SHA throttle is also cleared, so the (unbounded-cost) panel can be re-triggered on the same commit. Forged `<!-- agent-metric {json} -->` in evidence is additionally aggregated into the effort ledger. Mitigation: strip/escape `<!--` and `-->` (and the known marker prefixes) from every lens-supplied string before rendering.

samples.summary: `loc()` escapes the URL but not the link LABEL and never strips newlines from `file`, so a crafted `file` value injects arbitrary Markdown/HTML (including forged finding rows and off-site links) into the trusted App-authored review comment.
samples.evidence: loc() builds `[`${label}`](${url})` where `label` is the RAW `file` string (review-comment.mjs:56, 66). Only the URL half is percent-encoded (lines 63-65); the comment above it reasons carefully about `)`/`#`/`?` in the URL and overlooks the label entirely. A `file` of ``x`](https://evil.example) `` closes the code span, closes the link text at the unescaped `]`, and emits an attacker-chosen link plus arbitrary markup inside a comment authored by yorkie-agent[bot]. `f.file.trim()` (line 53) strips only leading/trailing whitespace, so embedded newlines survive (unlike `summary`, which is collapsed by `oneLine`), letting a single field inject whole new lines — e.g. `### Major (1)` followed by ``- `x.ts` — fake``, exactly the shape harvest.mjs:403-451 parses out of comments it trusts precisely because the author login is in PANEL_LOGINS (harvest.mjs:398, 472). `relocatedRow` has the same gap for `novelty.alsoAt` (line 118). Chain requires the lens to emit the crafted string (repo file name with backticks/brackets, or prompt-injected lens output), which is why confidence is low; impact if real is content spoofing of a trusted bot comment a maintainer reads to decide on merge. Fix: escape backticks/`]`/newlines in the label, or render the label via a sanitising helper.

samples.summary: Multi-line untrusted `evidence` is emitted as two-space-indented Markdown rather than inside a fenced block, so it renders as live Markdown/HTML (headings, links, images) in the bot comment.
samples.evidence:
`
  ${f.evidence.trim().replace(/
/g, "
  ")}
  </details>` (review-comment.mjs:98) indents by 2 spaces — not the 4 required for an indented code block — so every line of lens-supplied evidence is rendered as Markdown inside the `<details>`. Combined with the raw `<summary>` HTML around it, evidence containing `</details>` or a heading restructures the comment. Rendering evidence inside a fence (with the fence length chosen to exceed any backtick run in the text) would keep it inert while preserving readability.

samples.summary: No test exercises adversarial finding text: the new suite covers reserved characters only for URL encoding, never backticks/brackets/newlines in `file`, nor HTML-comment markers in `evidence`/`summary`.
samples.evidence: review-comment.test.mjs tests `loc` for `(`, `)`, `#`, `?`, space (lines 40-50) — all on the URL side — and asserts nothing about the label, about newline-bearing `file`, or about evidence/summary containing `<!--`/`-->`/`</details>`. Since this renderer's whole input is LLM output derived from the untrusted branch, a rendering test with hostile strings is the cheap regression guard for the two injection findings above. Note the repo's mechanical lanes run this suite but cannot prove it is adequate.
searchedFor: grep for backtick/newline/`<!--` cases in scripts/agent/review-comment.test.mjs

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out against the repository. review-comment.mjs:98 renders `f.evidence` verbatim (only re-indented) and :221 renders `l.summary.trim()` verbatim; `oneLine` (:45) only collapses whitespace, so `<!-- ... -->` markers pass through intact. No sanitizer exists in scripts/agent (severity.mjs:41 forwards `evidence` unchanged; the only scrub helpers are hunt-fingerprint/hunt-ui-probe, unrelated). The region is published as the App-authored comment together with the per-SHA throttle marker at agent-review-on-demand.yml:594-601 (marker defined :516, throttle checked :91-96). The SAME job then runs metrics.mjs summarize at :642, which lists comments at metrics.mjs:834 (after the post) and at :899 deletes EVERY comment whose body merely `includes(SUMMARY_MARKER)` — unanchored substring match, no author check (contrast harvest.mjs:377 which anchors its marker with ^). :908-915 additionally sweeps any body containing METRIC_PREFIX, and :845/:686 ingest any `<!-- agent-metrics-data ... -->` block into the ledger. So untrusted PR-derived text quoted as evidence crosses unescaped into a privileged marker-keyed control channel, causing self-deletion of the review comment, clearing of the per-SHA throttle (unbounded re-trigger of an expensive agent run), and forgeable metric records. This sits squarely in the injection / unsafe-input-handling lane, and is a real weakness rather than a correctness nit. Only exploit reliability (a lens must quote the planted string) is uncertain, and the self-inflicted variant — any finding quoting metrics.mjs:48's own marker constant — needs no attacker at all. No refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed. review-comment.mjs:53 does `f.file.trim()` (leading/trailing only — embedded newlines survive), :56 builds the label from the raw file string, :63-65 percent-encode ONLY the URL segments (the adjacent comment reasons about `)`/`#`/`?` in the URL and never mentions the label), and :66 interpolates the raw label into ``[`label`(url)]`` inside a single-backtick code span. A file value containing a backtick + `]` closes the span and link text and injects an attacker-chosen destination plus raw markup; embedded newlines inject whole new lines. relocatedRow at :118 has the identical gap for `novelty.alsoAt`. The downstream trust is real: harvest.mjs:398/:472 accept a comment because its author is the App, then parsePanelComment (:426-454) line-scans for `### Critical|Major` (:403) and `` - `file` — summary `` rows (:408), so injected lines are parsed as trusted panel findings that can suppress candidates. I found no guard: grepping every producer/consumer of finding.file (severity.mjs:39,80,105; review-panel.mjs:2352; rebuttal.mjs:88,125; novelty.mjs:151; harvest.mjs:551) and searching for any escaping helper (sanitiz|escapeMd|escapeMarkdown|stripHtml) returned nothing — rebuttal.mjs:88 only length-trims and novelty.mjs:151 only trims, so no upstream validation constrains `file` to a path shape. In-lane as injection / unsafe input handling with content-spoofing impact on a trusted App-authored comment. No not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.
